Article 3
Paragraph (1) Letter a Sufficiently Clear Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced work or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation of reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and or body tissue or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences incidents of violence and human rights violations Letter e Mediation is conducted for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.
Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/grabbing hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons, and/or resulting in disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
Letter b What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, comments that are hurtful or demeaning to self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.
Letter c What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets a person's body and sexuality, which results in or can result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis toward the victim's vagina, anus or mouth. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Molestation is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.
Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, imposing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household, forced sexual intercourse against someone in the household with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
Letter d What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or children or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working in a proper manner.
Letter e What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or children in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in the community as well as restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sigi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sigi.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the people's representative institution of Sigi Regency Region as an element of Regional government administration.
5. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Sigi Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
10. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
25. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 5
Letter a Sufficiently clear Letter b The basic rights referred to include the right to education and access to parents during the handling process Letter c What is meant by negative stigma is negative labeling (naming, symbolizing) by the public or society upon the victim which can result in the victim's alienation within their own community, including other mental pressures.
Letter d What is meant by freedom to determine choice after parental divorce is the legal consequence of the dissolution of marriage due to divorce. Based on the provisions in Article 41 of Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage ("Marriage Law") it is stated that the consequences of the dissolution of a marriage due to divorce are:
a. Both mother or father remain obligated to care for and educate their children, solely based on the interests of the child, if there is a dispute regarding custody of the children, the Court shall give its decision.
b. The father who is responsible for all maintenance and education costs required by the child, if the father in reality cannot fulfill such obligation the court may determine that the mother shall share such costs.
c. The Court may oblige the former husband to provide living costs and/or determine a certain obligation for the former wife.
The only regulation that clearly and explicitly provides guidance for judges in deciding the granting of custody rights over the child is found in Article 105 of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI) which states: "In the event of divorce:
a) custody of a child who is not yet mumayyiz or not yet 12 years old is the right of the mother.
b) custody of a child who is already mumayyiz is handed over to the child to choose between the father or mother as the holder of custody rights.
c) maintenance costs are borne by the father."

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by the right to have one's dignity respected is upholding human rights Letter b What is meant by the right to complaint handling is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers Letter c What is meant by the right to determine one's own decision is the right of the victim to choose the service action, the process to be undertaken, and the parties involved in handling their case.
Letter d What is meant by the right to information is the right to obtain information, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology both electronically and non-electronically related to acts of violence.
Letter e Sufficiently clear Letter f What is meant by the right to compensation includes economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills.
Letter g Sufficiently Clear Letter h What is meant by the right to assistance includes among others psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious counselors, advocates, and family members. Assistants are individuals who work as volunteers to provide protection and support to women and children victims of violence during the judicial process, these assistants can come from family members, friends or independent organizations that provide attention to witnesses and victims or advocates.
Letter i What is meant by the victim's right to rehabilitation includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights

Article 21
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children from victims of violence, which is organized by the Regional Government either directly or indirectly.

These provisions support a “Yes” for data collection/information systems, so the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

Article 9

Paragraph (1) Letter a Sufficiently Clear Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced work or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation of reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and or body tissue or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences incidents of violence and human rights violations Letter e Mediation is conducted for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.
Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/grabbing hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons, and/or resulting in disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
Letter b What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, comments that are hurtful or demeaning to self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.
Letter c What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets a person's body and sexuality, which results in or can result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis toward the victim's vagina, anus or mouth. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Molestation is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.
Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, imposing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household, forced sexual intercourse against someone in the household with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
Letter d What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or children or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working in a proper manner.
Letter e What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or children in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in the community as well as restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

Article 8
The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, include preventive actions, handling and recovery of women and children victims of acts of violence.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY
NUMBER 9 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Human Trafficking.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various matters, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that has not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and share the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by the right to have one's dignity respected is upholding human rights Letter b What is meant by the right to complaint handling is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers Letter c What is meant by the right to determine one's own decision is the right of the victim to choose the service action, the process to be undertaken, and the parties involved in handling their case.
Letter d What is meant by the right to information is the right to obtain information, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology both electronically and non-electronically related to acts of violence.
Letter e Sufficiently clear Letter f What is meant by the right to compensation includes economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills.
Letter g Sufficiently Clear Letter h What is meant by the right to assistance includes among others psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious counselors, advocates, and family members. Assistants are individuals who work as volunteers to provide protection and support to women and children victims of violence during the judicial process, these assistants can come from family members, friends or independent organizations that provide attention to witnesses and victims or advocates.
Letter i What is meant by the victim's right to rehabilitation includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by the principle of humanity is an existential state of humans as living beings with reason who are endowed with natural rights that are inherent and must be recognized, valued, and respected by every person, including specific aspects attached to women according to their gender, which in the process of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence must be respected and fulfilled by the state, among others including the human rights of women and children, protection and security as victims of violence, obtaining the best, affordable and fast services, sensitivity and empathy, and maintained confidentiality as victims of violence.
Letter b What is meant by the principle of justice is a mental state of every human being who naturally/inherently desires to obtain a sense of justice as part of society and/or the fulfillment of a sense of justice for every person in their position as citizens. In relation to the protection of women and children victims of violence whose implementation is regulated through this regional regulation, it must fulfill the principle of justice at least including gender equality, legal certainty, presumption of innocence, equality of rights before the law, not blaming the victim, the best interests of the victim. The meaning of the best interests of the victim is that in the process of handling cases experienced by victims, all parties involved in it, whether government, society, legislative, executive, judicial bodies must place the interests of the victim as the most important in all situations.
Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d Sufficiently Clear

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sigi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sigi.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the people's representative institution of Sigi Regency Region as an element of Regional government administration.
5. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Sigi Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
10. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
25. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 5
Letter a Sufficiently clear Letter b The basic rights referred to include the right to education and access to parents during the handling process Letter c What is meant by negative stigma is negative labeling (naming, symbolizing) by the public or society upon the victim which can result in the victim's alienation within their own community, including other mental pressures.
Letter d What is meant by freedom to determine choice after parental divorce is the legal consequence of the dissolution of marriage due to divorce. Based on the provisions in Article 41 of Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage ("Marriage Law") it is stated that the consequences of the dissolution of a marriage due to divorce are:
a. Both mother or father remain obligated to care for and educate their children, solely based on the interests of the child, if there is a dispute regarding custody of the children, the Court shall give its decision.
b. The father who is responsible for all maintenance and education costs required by the child, if the father in reality cannot fulfill such obligation the court may determine that the mother shall share such costs.
c. The Court may oblige the former husband to provide living costs and/or determine a certain obligation for the former wife.
The only regulation that clearly and explicitly provides guidance for judges in deciding the granting of custody rights over the child is found in Article 105 of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI) which states: "In the event of divorce:
a) custody of a child who is not yet mumayyiz or not yet 12 years old is the right of the mother.
b) custody of a child who is already mumayyiz is handed over to the child to choose between the father or mother as the holder of custody rights.
c) maintenance costs are borne by the father."

6.2.rationale: The Indonesian text references the anti-trafficking law in the “Mengingat” section (UU No. 21 Tahun 2007) and in the General Elucidation, and the Elucidation to Pasal 3 defines “eksploitasi.” But the operative provisions of the Perda define “Korban” as women/children victims of “kekerasan” and set out services for violence victims; it does not specifically identify trafficking victims as a distinct group or provide trafficking-specific measures. Citing the existence of a legal reference/definition as proof that trafficking victims are covered as an intersectional category is an overreach by the judge. Thus, the judge’s reasoning was too lenient given what the regulation actually regulates.

6.9.translated_snippet:
THE ROLE OF CUSTOMARY INSTITUTIONS IN THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
(1) Customary institutions that provide services for the resolution of cases of violence against women and children who are victims of acts of violence may carry out their functions in accordance with applicable customary provisions as long as they do not conflict with the principles and objectives stipulated in this Regional Regulation.
6.9.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly addresses the role of customary institutions and allows customary institutions to provide services for resolving cases of violence against women and children victims, indicating inclusion of customary (adat) community mechanisms within the protection framework.

CHAPTER VIII
THE ROLE OF CUSTOMARY INSTITUTIONS IN THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 15
(1) Customary institutions that provide services for the resolution of cases of violence against women and children who are victims of acts of violence may carry out their functions in accordance with applicable customary provisions as long as they do not conflict with the principles and objectives stipulated in this Regional Regulation.
(2) Certain cases that have consequences for criminal acts based on positive law related to the service functions of customary institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be transferred to the competent authorities.
(3) Decisions and sanctions regarding cases of violence against women and children other than the provisions regulated in paragraph (2) that are produced through customary courts may be implemented in accordance with local customary provisions.

Article 11
Preventive actions against violence towards women and children implemented by the community may take the form of:
a. active participation in programs and activities initiated by the Government, Regional Government, or other parties as long as they do not contradict the principles of protection for women and children stipulated in this Regional Regulation;
b. activities initiated by the community as long as they do not contradict the principles of protection for women and children stipulated in this Regional Regulation.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 9

c. conduct independent socialization of women's and children's rights; d. provide first aid to victims; and
e. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.

6.9.rationale: The original Indonesian text (BAB VIII, Pasal 15) regulates “Peran Lembaga Adat” (role of customary institutions) in resolving cases, including referral to competent authorities for criminal cases. This acknowledges customary institutions, but it does not explicitly address “indigenous groups” (kelompok masyarakat adat/indigenous peoples) as a vulnerable population category with tailored protections; it is more about dispute-resolution fora/mechanisms. The judge treated ‘customary institutions’ as equivalent to ‘indigenous groups inclusion,’ which is a category-mapping error (too broad interpretation) rather than missing evidence.
